learningObjectives.title: Probability of single events and the probability scale
Sample spaces, Venn and tree diagrams

questions.q: The probability of an event is always a number between which two values?
questions.explain: All probabilities lie on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

questions.q: For an event A, the probability that A does not happen is equal to:
questions.explain: The probabilities of an event happening and not happening always sum to 1.

questions.q: If a set of outcomes is mutually exclusive and exhaustive, their probabilities sum to:
questions.explain: Exhaustive outcomes cover every possibility, so their probabilities total 1.

questions.q: To find the probability that two independent events both occur, you should:
questions.explain: For independent events the AND rule gives P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

questions.q: For two mutually exclusive events A and B, the probability of A or B is found by:
questions.explain: Mutually exclusive events cannot both occur, so P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

questions.q: Expected frequency of an outcome is calculated as:
questions.explain: The expected number of occurrences is the probability multiplied by how many trials take place.

questions.q: Relative frequency (experimental probability) is calculated as:
options: Number of successful trials ÷ total number of trials
Total number of trials ÷ number of successful trials
Number of successful trials × total number of trials
Number of successful trials - total number of trials
questions.explain: Relative frequency estimates probability from experimental results as successes over total trials.

questions.q: A list or diagram showing all possible outcomes of an experiment is called a:
questions.explain: The sample space is the complete set of all possible outcomes.

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
questions.explain: Three of the six equally likely outcomes (2, 4, 6) are even, giving 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.q: The probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.3. What is the probability that it does not rain?
Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events, P(A or B) = 0.2 + 0.5 = 0.7.

questions.q: As an experiment is repeated many more times, the relative frequency estimate of a probability generally becomes:
options: A more reliable estimate of the true probability
Exactly equal to the theoretical value every time
Completely unaffected by the number of trials
questions.explain: More trials give a relative frequency that tends to settle closer to the true probability.

questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.explain: The sample space is HH, HT, TH, TT, so P(two heads) = 1/4.

questions.q: In a Venn diagram, the intersection of sets A and B represents outcomes that are:
options: In A or B but not both
questions.explain: The intersection contains elements belonging to A and B at the same time.

questions.q: Two counters are taken from a bag one after the other without replacement. The two events are:
questions.explain: Without replacement the first outcome changes the second probability, so the events are dependent.

questions.q: A spinner can land on red, blue or green only. P(red) = 0.4 and P(blue) = 0.35. What is P(green)?
questions.explain: The probabilities are exhaustive and sum to 1, so P(green) = 1 - 0.4 - 0.35 = 0.25.

questions.q: A bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. One ball is taken at random. What is the probability it is red?
questions.explain: There are 3 red out of 5 balls in total, so P(red) = 3/5.

questions.q: Two independent events have probabilities 0.5 and 0.2. What is the probability that both occur?
questions.explain: For independent events, P(both) = 0.5 × 0.2 = 0.1.

questions.q: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue counters. Two are taken without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
A spinner lands on red with probability 0.25. In 80 spins, what is the expected number of reds?
questions.explain: Expected frequency = 0.25 × 80 = 20.
